customManagers.description: Track the vendored HetrixTools agent version (re-vendor on bump). Renovate compiles matchStrings with only the `g` flag, so `$` means end of file: the earlier `^(?<currentValue>.*)$` never matched a file ending in a newline, and this dependency was never detected. `\s*$` allows the trailing newline, and the digits pin it to a release number, which the Lint step requires too.

Track the bats-core that Lint installs from GitHub (.github/workflows/lint.yaml, step 'Install bats'). It lives here rather than in the shared preset because that preset's `# renovate:` annotation manager carries only a version, and this pin is a version plus the commit it resolves to: the commit is what the step fetches, the version is what Renovate compares. Both are captured in one match, so a bump rewrites them together. BATS_COMMIT is the commit the annotated tag points to, never the tag object's own SHA. The fields are joined with `[ \t]` and exactly one `\n`, not `\s`, so a match cannot run across into a neighbouring block (owine/renovate-config PR #4). tests/renovate-config.bats checks this pattern against the real file.

packageRules.description: Alpine apk pins are extracted by Renovate's built-in dockerfile manager (>= 44.96.0) as datasource `apk`; the :alpine preset supplies the grouping, rangeStrategy and automerge posture but stays release-line agnostic, so this URL is where the Alpine release line is written for Renovate. Bump `branch=v3.24` when the base image crosses a release line (3.24 -> 3.25), together with `alpine-branch` in .github/workflows/apk-arch-rerun.yaml (the only other place the line is named). `components=main,community` merges both indexes in a single lookup (registryStrategy 'merge'), so community packages need no separate registryUrls override.

Vendored HetrixTools agent — NEVER automerge, at any update type. The bump only moves the `upstream-agent.version` marker; the agent script itself is vendored in-tree and must be re-fetched by hand with the `>>> ha-app patch >>>` patches (dry_run, SID kept out of diagnostics, ping RTT passed to awk as data, raw probe output logged indented, TCP probe target passed as arguments) re-applied and upstream-agent.sha256 / upstream-agent.patches updated (see hetrixtools-agent/DOCS.md); Lint's 'vendored agent vs upstream' step fails until that is done. Without this rule the marker is swept into :automerge's 'all non-major dependencies' bundle and merged unattended, leaving the marker claiming a version the vendored script isn't.

The ONE `feat:` in this repo's Renovate surface, and a deliberate exception to the fleet rule that no dependency update is ever typed `feat:` (see owine/renovate-config's README). It holds here because this app is a packaging shim: its whole output is the HetrixTools agent, so the version a user runs IS this dependency's version — the question Renovate can't normally answer ("is this bump consumer-visible?") has a fixed answer of yes. Scoped to minor/major only so an upstream PATCH stays `deps:` (patch release) instead of cutting a minor here: the app's semver then tracks upstream's own update type rather than drifting a digit ahead of it. The `feat:` lands only when the re-vendor commit does, since the rule above blocks automerge.

home-assistant/builder actions: NEVER automerge. On a release they run with `packages: write` and `id-token: write` (they push and cosign-sign the image HA pulls), and a digest bump can silently move the build runner OS (see the note on the Build matrix step in .github/workflows/build.yaml). So read the action source at the new digest before merging. Renovate's packageName for `home-assistant/builder/actions/<name>@sha` is `home-assistant/builder`, so this covers every builder action. Its own group keeps it out of :automerge's 'all non-major ci dependencies' group, where one non-automerge member would hold back every other CI update. Known limit: :default's vulnerabilityAlerts sets automerge after packageRules, so a security-advisory PR for the builder would still automerge.
